summary: This revision fixes the structural gap I raised: section 7 introduces a genuinely good four-value evidence policy (available = verified on the locally installed version, inferred = docs/source only, unavailable, fallback) with a stated evidence basis per backend, section 9 adds the mandated 3x3 backend-by-route matrix, every Paseo cell is marked inferred, and the migration plan gates the Paseo skill behind a named local validation matrix. On epistemic labeling it is now better than Proposal 2, and that vocabulary is worth adopting. But the framework is applied without probing, and the result is a verified false negative in the core matrix: section 9.1 records Claude Code 'Persisted automatic goal: unavailable' and routes Claude to the weaker fallback, whereas the installed claude 2.1.222 binary contains /goal, '/goal active', '/goal clear to stop early', '/goal <condition> to set another', plus getStopHookMessage, executeStopHooks, stopHookActive and stopHookBlockingCount — a native condition-based goal built on Stop hooks that restores on --resume. It also still misses ~/.codex/goals_1.sqlite (thread_goals with objective, six statuses, token_budget, tokens_used, time_used_seconds), so goal activation is still verified by scraping 'visible Codex goal UI' on the alternate screen it declares unreliable, and Codex-route token telemetry is recorded as unavailable. Three prior findings remain unrepaired for a third round: section 11 still resolves lost Herdr output by asking the reviewer to reproduce its previous message 'verbatim' (retrospective regeneration against a hard criterion, with the agent_session transcript pointer still unmentioned); section 6 still prefers key-level send-keys for /goal though the installed skill documents agent prompt as atomic and bracketed-paste-aware; and adopt-project still has no audit verdict, with no mo-setup equivalent, leaving project onboarding (linter configs, docs layout, AGENTS.md fragment) unowned. The mo-qc/mo-e2e exit-2 ambiguity and the absent review-loop convergence rule also persist.

blocking_findings.area: Claude Code goal capability — verified false negative
blocking_findings.description: Section 9.1 asserts 'Persisted automatic goal: unavailable — equivalent не подтверждён' for the Claude Code route, and section 6 lists Claude Code among surfaces requiring the weaker persistent-session fallback. Strings extracted from the installed /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code@latest/2.1.222/claude include '/goal', '/goal active', '/goal clear to stop early', '/goal <condition> to set another', '/goal <condition> to set one', '/goal is only available in trusted workspaces', '/goal can't run while hooks are restricted (disableAllHooks or allowManagedHooksOnly ...)', together with getStopHookMessage, executeStopHooks, stopHookActive and stopHookBlockingCount in the query loop alongside turnCount/maxTurns. Claude Code has a native session-scoped condition-based goal implemented over Stop hooks that restores on --resume/--continue. The assertion drives the design to a weaker mechanism on the route the user's own wrapper configures.
blocking_findings.required_change: Test rather than assume this cell; record Claude Code /goal as available with its real preconditions (trusted workspace, hooks not restricted by disableAllHooks or allowManagedHooksOnly, condition must be judgeable from Claude's own output because the evaluator cannot read files or run commands, hence a turn bound is required), and remove Claude Code from the fallback-only list.

blocking_findings.description: Third round unrepaired. Section 11's Herdr path still asks the reviewer to write its previous message 'verbatim' to a Markdown file after the panel read fails. If the panel lost it, the model's own context may have been compacted, so this regenerates rather than retrieves — silently paraphrasing, compressing and dropping caveats, against the hard criterion that full reviewer messages must not be lost. Ignored verified alternatives: agent_session appears in the Herdr API schema, ~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh populates transcript pointers, and ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl plus ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl hold authoritative transcripts. A prospective write-to-file instruction is also strictly better than a retrospective re-export.
blocking_findings.required_change: Make retrieval prospective (worker writes its complete answer to a file as part of its task and returns only the path) and add reading the route's own transcript JSONL as the non-generative secondary path; demote retrospective re-export to last resort and label it as regeneration, not verbatim retrieval.

blocking_findings.area: Codex goal state and telemetry channel
blocking_findings.description: Goal activation is confirmed via 'visible Codex goal UI', i.e. reading the alternate screen the document itself marks unreliable for content, and the Codex route rows record context/last-turn signals as unavailable. ~/.codex/goals_1.sqlite ships migrated tables thread_goals(thread_id, goal_id, objective, status IN active|paused|blocked|usage_limited|budget_limited|complete, token_budget, tokens_used, time_used_seconds, created_at_ms, updated_at_ms) and thread_goal_continuation_deferrals, providing queryable activation confirmation and real consumption metrics with no new artifact, and directly answering Q24's 'без нового goal.json, FSM или proxy CLI'. usage_limited/budget_limited also map onto the subscription-exhaustion trigger in task section 4.1, and paused/deferrals bear on the goal-granularity choice.
blocking_findings.required_change: Verify and monitor goal state from the harness's own goal store; upgrade the Codex-route telemetry cells accordingly; re-evaluate goal granularity in light of native pause/deferral; note the layout is version-specific and must be re-probed rather than hardcoded.

blocking_findings.area: goal input mechanism contradicted by installed skill
blocking_findings.description: Section 6 states '/goal вводится native key-level input с отдельным Enter' and treats a framed prompt as unreliable. The installed herdr --skill states verbatim that 'agent prompt atomically submits text and encoded Enter while honoring the pane's live bracketed-paste mode'. The rejected mechanism is the atomic one; send-keys with a separate Enter is likelier to split the slash command. The skill also documents that --wait tracks lifecycle state rather than turn boundaries, which the premature-idle logic depends on and which is unmentioned.
blocking_findings.required_change: Use agent prompt for goal submission per the installed skill, and require waiting for idle before prompting because --wait may be satisfied by completion of an already-active turn.

blocking_findings.area: audit completeness, project onboarding owner, mo-qc contract
blocking_findings.description: adopt-project still receives no keep/replace/delete/defer verdict for a third round despite section 22 auditing individual test fixtures, and with no mo-setup equivalent nobody owns project onboarding (installing linter configs, creating the docs layout, inserting the AGENTS.md fragment) beyond 'executor добавляет aliases'. Separately, agent-required mo-e2e is specified to print AGENT_REQUIRED and exit 2 while mo-qc is the recommended aggregate, but it is never stated whether mo-qc includes mo-e2e (if so, standard make semantics fail every QC run in agent-E2E projects), and the exit-2 sentinel has no named machine consumer although manifests were deleted for exactly that reason. The review loop also has no convergence rule for the case where each new revision surfaces fresh findings.
blocking_findings.required_change: Add a verdict for adopt-project and assign project onboarding to a named owner; state explicitly that mo-qc must not depend on an agent-required mo-e2e and either name the exit-2 consumer or drop the sentinel; add a convergence rule routing residual non-blocking findings to docs/todo.md.

assumptions: The absent paseo CLI reflects the real target environment, which this revision now handles correctly by marking all Paseo cells inferred.
Reading ~/.codex and ~/.claude state files read-only is an acceptable methodology mechanism, introducing no new artifact or protocol.
String extraction from the installed Claude Code binary is sound evidence that /goal exists in 2.1.222; I did not execute /goal end to end.
